Extend inference reach beyond managed APIs to self-hosted production infrastructure using Red Hat AI Enterprise, establishing enterprise control over token economics, data sovereignty, and multi-environment consistency while preserving managed APIs for development and frontier model access.

Deploy a Kubernetes-native inference platform with KServe model serving, vLLM inference engines, Connectivity Link API governance, and comprehensive observability, then progressively extend production workloads through a Crawl-Walk-Run adoption lifecycle using parallel-run validation and evidence-based workload tiering.

narratives.name: Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why extending inference reach from managed APIs to self-hosted infrastructure is strategically necessary.

narrativeContexts.context: Extending AI inference from managed API consumption to self-hosted production infrastructure is a strategic endeavor that addresses four interconnected value pillars -- full-stack control, data sovereignty, platform consistency, and token economics -- while preserving managed APIs as a complementary tier for development and frontier model capabilities.

The expansion endeavor operates on a coexistence model where Bedrock serves development, prototyping, and frontier model access while RHAIE provides production-scale inference with enterprise control. The economic crossover point at approximately 10,000-20,000 requests per day defines where self-hosted inference becomes more cost-effective, with agent token amplification potentially lowering this threshold by 5-10x.

Devopsity demonstrates 60-80% cost reduction at 500,000 requests per day with self-hosted inference. Spheron identifies the break-even at 50-100 million tokens per month. Gartner projects 40% of agentic AI projects canceled due to unsustainable costs. IDC confirms 64% of infrastructure leaders already operate hybrid infrastructure. NVIDIA estimates 55-80% of enterprise GPU spend goes to inference. These converging data points establish inference expansion as both economically compelling and strategically necessary.

The expansion from managed API consumption to self-hosted production inference follows a progressive Crawl-Walk-Run lifecycle, building team capability and organizational confidence through increasingly complex workload waves while maintaining managed APIs for workloads where they remain the optimal choice.

narratives.name: Placement Decision Framework
narratives.description: How workload placement uses four-class categorization to optimize inference tier assignment.

narrativeContexts.context: Workload placement strategy provides the decision framework for routing each AI inference workload to the most appropriate tier, using four-class categorization (Quick Wins, Strategic Expansion, Low-Risk Testing, Defer) informed by volume, sensitivity, complexity, and provider dependency analysis.

Begin by extracting per-application telemetry from managed API usage (CloudWatch logs, billing records). Profile token characteristics including agent amplification factors. Apply the four-class framework using cost-crossover analysis at approximately 10,000-20,000 requests per day. Assign migration waves starting with stateless classifiers (Wave 1) through high-volume variable-traffic APIs (Wave 4). Validate each transition through parallel-run before production cutover. Review classification quarterly.

Using aggregate billing data without per-application granularity obscures which workloads have crossed the crossover threshold. Ignoring agent token amplification understates actual costs by 5-10x. Forcing all workloads to self-hosted inference when some benefit from managed API convenience and frontier capabilities. Treating classification as one-time rather than continuous as volume patterns and economics evolve.

narratives.description: How unified OpenAI-compatible interfaces with Connectivity Link governance enable transparent inference consumption.

narrativeContexts.context: The API Consistency Layer provides unified, OpenAI-compatible interfaces for inference consumption across managed APIs and self-hosted environments, with enterprise governance through Connectivity Link (Kuadrant) providing authentication via Authorino, token-based rate limiting via Limitador, and comprehensive usage metering.

Deploy vLLM with OpenAI-compatible endpoints to establish standard interfaces. Refactor application code from boto3 invoke_model calls to OpenAI SDK with configurable base_url and api_key. Deploy Connectivity Link with AuthPolicy for API key validation and TokenRateLimitPolicy for tier-based token consumption limits. Configure Limitador to extract total_tokens from response bodies. Implement per-user counters using Authorino-injected identity metadata. Enable showback reporting from Limitador Prometheus metrics.

Maintaining separate SDK integrations for managed and self-hosted endpoints instead of standardizing on OpenAI-compatible interfaces. Implementing request-count rate limiting instead of token-based rate limiting, which fails to account for the variable cost of AI inference requests. Neglecting to measure agent token amplification, causing rate limits to be set too permissively for agentic workloads.

Deployment risk encompasses seven interconnected vectors identified through source methodology analysis and industry research. GPU resource risks (OOM failures during concurrency spikes), network risks (congestion in disaggregated architectures), security risks (cross-namespace bypass as demonstrated by CVE-2025-12805), storage risks (accidental bucket deletion), financial risks (agent token amplification), skills risks (team capability gaps during transition), and quality risks (model regression during tier transition).

NTT DATA research reveals 95% of enterprises consider sovereignty important but only 29% are implementing it. MIT Technology Review demonstrates 0.93 correlation between sovereignty commitment and AI program success. CVE-2025-12805 demonstrates real-world consequences of inadequate namespace isolation in inference environments. Gartner projects 40% of agentic AI projects canceled due to cost overruns, emphasizing financial risk from unmanaged token economics.

A comprehensive risk profile that evolves through identification, assessment, mitigation, and continuous management provides the governance foundation that enables the organization to extend inference reach confidently, knowing that each risk vector has been addressed with appropriate controls and ongoing monitoring.

Inventory current managed API models from the usage baseline. Identify candidates from Llama, Granite, Sentence-Transformers, and other families based on published benchmarks and parameter counts. Calculate minimum GPU requirements using the standard memory formula accounting for parameters, precision bytes, 20% overhead, tensor parallelism, and PagedAttention buffers. Run candidates against representative production prompts. Evaluate quality using automated metrics supplemented by human review for critical workloads. Document remain on managed API decisions where quality parity is not achievable.

Relying solely on academic benchmark scores without testing representative production prompts. Assuming all managed API models have adequate open-weight equivalents. Neglecting to validate compressed model variants under concurrent production load.

activities.name: Engineer Hardware Profiles and GPU Configurations
activities.description: Design GPU node configurations, tensor parallelism, and memory allocation for target models.

narratives.name: Hardware Profile Engineering Technique
narratives.description: How model requirements translate into validated GPU node configurations.

narrativeContexts.context: Hardware profile engineering translates model requirements into specific GPU node configurations balancing performance, cost, and operational complexity, producing decision matrices that map each model to validated deployment configurations across multiple hardware options.

Specify complete hardware profiles per model including GPU model and count, tensor parallelism factor, maximum context length, GPU memory utilization target, and compute precision. Apply model quantization using LLM Compressor for INT8 and AWQ variants to enable deployment on smaller GPU configurations. Deploy NVIDIA GPU Operator and Node Feature Discovery for GPU lifecycle management. Validate profiles through sustained-load benchmarking including burst testing at peak concurrency. Document multi-model sharing configurations and edge deployment profiles.

Over-provisioning GPU resources based on worst-case estimates without empirical validation under realistic concurrent load. Neglecting burst testing that reveals OOM failures not apparent in steady-state benchmarks. Specifying configurations without considering multi-model sharing scenarios.

activities.name: Deploy Model Registry and Storage Infrastructure
activities.description: Provision S3-compatible storage and Model Registry for open-weight model management.

narratives.name: Model Registry Deployment Technique
narratives.description: How to establish the system of record for model weights and deployment metadata.

narrativeContexts.context: Deploy Model Registry and Storage Infrastructure establishes the system of record for model weights, versions, and deployment metadata using S3-compatible object storage and the OpenShift AI Model Registry with external database backend.

Configure DataScienceCluster with Model Registry set to Managed. Deploy external MySQL or PostgreSQL database for persistent metadata. Provision S3 storage via ODF NooBaa for in-cluster or external S3 for cross-environment access. Download open-weight model weights in SafeTensors format and register via REST API with artifact URI lineage. Validate that model storage lifecycle is independent of cluster namespace management by testing namespace deletion in development environments.

Storing production model weights in ObjectBucketClaims tied to namespace lifecycles, risking cascade deletion when namespaces are cleaned up. Neglecting to include the Model Registry database in disaster recovery backup scope.

activities.name: Configure Model Serving via KServe
activities.description: Deploy and validate model serving infrastructure using KServe with production-grade runtimes.

narratives.name: KServe Configuration Technique
narratives.description: How KServe ServingRuntime and InferenceService custom resources deploy inference endpoints.

narrativeContexts.context: Configure Model Serving translates hardware profiles into running inference endpoints by creating KServe ServingRuntime and InferenceService custom resources with vLLM or Caikit+TGIS runtimes in RawDeployment mode.

Create ServingRuntime manifests specifying the vLLM container image, startup arguments (model path, tensor parallel size, maximum model length, GPU memory utilization, data type), and resource limits. Create InferenceService manifests linking model storage URIs to serving runtimes. Use RawDeployment mode to avoid Knative cold-start latencies. Configure health probes using vLLM health endpoints rather than simple TCP checks. Validate API compatibility by confirming OpenAI-compatible chat completion and token usage reporting in response bodies.

Using Knative Serverless mode, which introduces cold-start latencies inappropriate for production inference. Setting readiness probes as TCP port checks instead of model-loading health endpoints. Neglecting to plan for model version update rollout strategies that account for multi-minute model loading times.

activities.name: Implement API Gateway and Governance Layer
activities.description: Deploy authentication, token-based rate limiting, and traffic management for inference endpoints.

narratives.name: API Gateway Implementation Technique
narratives.description: How Connectivity Link deploys three-stage API governance for inference endpoints.

narrativeContexts.context: Implement API Gateway and Governance Layer deploys Connectivity Link (Kuadrant) with three-stage architecture: Envoy proxy for traffic interception, Authorino for identity validation and metadata injection, and Limitador for token-based rate limiting with per-user consumption tracking.

Configure Gateway and HTTPRoute resources for inference endpoint routing. Deploy AuthPolicy with Authorino validating API keys against Kubernetes secrets with OIDC and mTLS support. Deploy TokenRateLimitPolicy with Limitador extracting total_tokens from OpenAI-compatible response bodies and enforcing per-user tier-based limits. Configure counters expressions to isolate limits using Authorino-injected identity metadata. Enable Limitador Prometheus metrics for showback reporting. Configure governance for all inference environments with GitOps synchronization.

Implementing traditional request-count rate limiting instead of token-based, which fails to account for the variable cost of AI inference requests. Neglecting to configure identity metadata injection, preventing per-user cost attribution. Failing to synchronize governance policies across environments through GitOps.

activities.name: Profile and Optimize Inference Performance
activities.description: Systematically benchmark, analyze, and optimize inference throughput and latency.

narratives.name: Performance Optimization Technique
narratives.description: How automated benchmarking with targeted optimizations achieves and exceeds managed API baselines.

narrativeContexts.context: Performance profiling combines automated benchmarking with analytical investigation of bottlenecks, applying targeted optimizations including PagedAttention tuning, model quantization, tensor parallelism, and advanced routing architectures to achieve and exceed managed API performance baselines.

Configure Prometheus to scrape vLLM engine and DCGM GPU metrics. Run automated benchmarks replicating production token characteristics and concurrency patterns. Measure TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queue depth, and cache utilization at multiple concurrency levels. Apply targeted optimizations -- adjust GPU memory utilization targets, tune PagedAttention buffer sizes, modify context lengths, apply quantization, configure continuous batching parameters. Validate each optimization through before-and-after benchmarking. Deploy llm-d for prefix-cache-aware scheduling. Configure disaggregated prefill-decode for highest-volume models.

Benchmarking with single-request latency instead of multi-tenant concurrent load. Treating performance optimization as one-time rather than continuous as workload patterns evolve. Applying quantization without empirically validating quality under concurrent load.

activities.name: Establish Operational Observability Stack
activities.description: Deploy multi-tier monitoring, SLO definitions, and alerting for inference services.

narratives.name: Observability Stack Deployment Technique
narratives.description: How three-tier monitoring covers GPU hardware, serving engine, and governance metrics.

narrativeContexts.context: Establish Operational Observability Stack deploys three-tier monitoring covering GPU hardware (DCGM exporter), serving engine (vLLM Prometheus metrics), and governance (Limitador counters) with SLO-based alerting and capacity planning dashboards.

Deploy NVIDIA DCGM exporter across GPU-enabled nodes for hardware metrics. Configure Prometheus scraping of vLLM endpoints for inference metrics. Integrate Limitador counters for token consumption and rate limiting metrics. Define SLOs for TTFT p99, throughput, availability, and error rate. Configure burn-rate alerting with multi-window analysis. Build Grafana dashboards for GPU infrastructure, model serving, and governance views. Deploy the OpenShift AI 3.4 usage dashboard for consolidated visibility.

Implementing cause-based alerting (alerting on GPU metric fluctuations) instead of symptom-based alerting (alerting on user-visible degradation). Not accounting for GPU workload startup time in on-call runbooks, leading to ineffective response procedures.

activities.name: Enforce Tenant Isolation and Security Controls
activities.description: Implement zero-trust namespace isolation, RBAC, and network security for inference workloads.

narratives.name: Tenant Isolation Technique
narratives.description: How zero-trust security operates across network, identity, and container layers.

narrativeContexts.context: Enforce Tenant Isolation implements zero-trust security across three layers -- network isolation (NetworkPolicies), identity and access management (RBAC, Authorino), and container security (image scanning, SCCs) -- with continuous validation through automated compliance scans and penetration testing.

Deploy default-deny NetworkPolicies with explicit allow rules for required paths (inference pods to S3, gateway to inference, monitoring scraping, DNS). Configure RBAC with least privilege for model operators, API consumers, and administrators. Apply Security Context Constraints restricting privilege escalation and filesystem access. Scan inference container images for vulnerabilities. Monitor CVEs affecting the inference stack. Validate isolation through penetration testing including cross-namespace access attempts.

Treating security as a bolt-on rather than designing it in from the beginning. Failing to monitor CVEs for the inference stack, as demonstrated by CVE-2025-12805 enabling cross-namespace authentication bypass. Deploying inference without custom SecurityContextConstraints.

activities.name: Validate Disaster Recovery Procedures
activities.description: Implement and regularly test backup and recovery for inference environments.

narratives.name: DR Validation Technique
narratives.description: How backup implementation with regular recovery testing ensures inference platform resilience.

narrativeContexts.context: Validate Disaster Recovery Procedures combines backup implementation with regular recovery testing, ensuring the inference platform can be restored within defined RTO targets including model serving configurations, registry state, governance policies, and model weights.

Configure backup workflows using Trilio or equivalent capturing namespace definitions, ServingRuntime and InferenceService manifests, secrets, and Model Registry database state. Back up model weights through S3-native replication. Ensure production model weights are stored in S3 buckets with lifecycles independent of namespace management. Execute recovery dry-runs in alternate namespaces verifying complete restoration. Measure end-to-end recovery time from restore initiation to successful inference response. Address bottlenecks if recovery exceeds RTO.

Omitting S3 credentials and secrets from backup scope. Storing production model weights in ObjectBucketClaims tied to namespace lifecycles. Testing recovery at component level without end-to-end validation of the complete inference stack.

activities.name: Configure Intelligent Workload Routing
activities.description: Deploy llm-d scheduler with prefix-cache-aware routing and disaggregated execution.

narratives.name: Intelligent Routing Technique
narratives.description: How llm-d prefix-cache-aware scheduling and disaggregated execution optimize inference.

narrativeContexts.context: Configure Intelligent Workload Routing deploys the llm-d project for prefix-cache-aware scheduling via the Endpoint Picker (EPP) filter-score-pick pipeline and optionally enables disaggregated prefill-decode execution with purpose-optimized GPU pools.

Deploy the EPP scheduler between API gateway and backend inference replicas. Configure the filter stage to remove unhealthy replicas, score stage to evaluate prefix cache match affinity and load, and pick stage to select optimal replicas. For disaggregated execution, deploy prefill-optimized replicas on high-compute GPUs (H100) and decode-optimized replicas on cost-effective GPUs (L40S). Configure KV-cache transfer via NixlConnector or LMCacheConnector. Validate through benchmarking that tail latency reduces 25-40% compared to co-located execution.

Deploying disaggregated execution without validating network bandwidth between GPU pools, causing KV-cache transfer bottlenecks. Neglecting to tune the prefill-to-decode pool sizing ratio based on workload prompt-to-completion length characteristics.

activities.name: Compress and Quantize Models
activities.description: Apply systematic model compression to reduce GPU memory while preserving quality.

narratives.name: Model Compression Technique
narratives.description: How quantization techniques reduce GPU memory while maintaining quality within thresholds.

narrativeContexts.context: Model compression applies quantization techniques (INT8, AWQ, FP8, INT4) using LLM Compressor and GuideLLM to reduce GPU memory requirements by 50-75% while maintaining quality within defined degradation thresholds.

Use LLM Compressor to generate INT8, AWQ, and FP8 quantized variants. For each compressed variant, run comprehensive quality benchmarks against full-precision models using representative production prompts and standard academic benchmarks. Define quality degradation thresholds before compression (maximum 2% accuracy degradation for FP8). Register validated compressed models in Model Registry with lineage linking to source models and compression metadata.

Applying compression without per-model quality validation, as some models degrade significantly at INT4. Evaluating only single-request quality without testing under concurrent load, where compressed models may exhibit different latency characteristics. Treating compression as one-time rather than iterating as new models enter the portfolio.

activities.name: Integrate Application Code for Dual-Endpoint Access
activities.description: Refactor application code to support both managed API and self-hosted inference endpoints.

narratives.name: Application Integration Technique
narratives.description: How application code refactors from provider-specific SDKs to standardized OpenAI-compatible interfaces.

narrativeContexts.context: Application code integration refactors from provider-specific SDK calls (boto3 invoke_model) to the standard OpenAI Python SDK with configurable base_url, enabling transparent backend switching between managed APIs and self-hosted endpoints through configuration rather than code changes.

Replace boto3 Bedrock-specific API calls with OpenAI SDK client initialized with configurable base_url and api_key environment variables. Implement parallel-run validation by sending duplicate requests to both tiers and comparing response quality, latency, and token usage. Execute gradual traffic cutover (5% to 25% to 50% to 75% to 100%) with monitoring at each level. Maintain managed APIs as fallback for burst capacity and frontier capabilities.

Maintaining separate SDK integrations instead of standardizing on OpenAI-compatible interfaces. Performing full cutover without parallel-run validation. Not maintaining managed API fallback capability after transition.

activities.name: Implement GitOps Platform Governance
activities.description: Manage all inference infrastructure as declarative code with automated reconciliation.

narratives.name: GitOps Governance Technique
narratives.description: How declarative infrastructure management provides consistency, auditability, and recoverability.

narrativeContexts.context: GitOps Platform Governance packages all inference infrastructure as Helm charts or Kustomize overlays managed through Argo CD, providing consistency across environments, auditability through Git history, recoverability from version control, and automated drift detection with correction.

Package namespace definitions, ServingRuntime and InferenceService manifests, Gateway API resources, AuthPolicy and TokenRateLimitPolicy, NetworkPolicies, RBAC, and monitoring configurations as declarative manifests. Configure Argo CD ApplicationSets for automatic synchronization. Establish pull request review workflow with role-appropriate reviewers. Create environment-specific overlays for staging and production. Enable drift detection with automatic correction.

Allowing manual cluster configuration changes that create drift from the declared state. Failing to include secrets management in the GitOps workflow. Not differentiating environment overlays, leading to either over-specification or under-specification per environment.

activities.name: Classify and Tier Inference Workloads
activities.description: Categorize AI workloads by complexity and impact to determine optimal inference tier.

narratives.name: Workload Classification Technique
narratives.description: How four-class prioritization framework assigns each workload to its optimal inference tier.

narrativeContexts.context: Workload classification applies the four-class prioritization framework (Quick Wins, Strategic Expansion, Low-Risk Testing, Defer) to each AI workload based on business impact, architectural complexity, volume profile, data sensitivity, and provider-specific feature dependencies.

Assess each workload across four dimensions -- volume (daily token consumption against cost crossover threshold), sensitivity (data classification and regulatory requirements), complexity (API patterns, concurrency, latency requirements), and dependencies (provider-specific features without standard equivalents). Assign workloads to four classes and migration waves (1-4) per workload. Maintain classification as a living document updated quarterly.

Using aggregate billing data to make workload-level decisions. Treating classification as a one-time exercise rather than continuous. Ignoring seasonal volume patterns where periodic peaks cross cost thresholds. Forcing all workloads to self-hosted when some benefit from managed API convenience.

activities.name: Assess Privacy and Sovereignty Requirements
activities.description: Evaluate data sovereignty and privacy requirements across inference workloads.

narratives.name: Privacy Assessment Technique
narratives.description: How regulatory requirements and data sensitivity map to workload placement decisions.

narrativeContexts.context: Privacy and sovereignty assessment maps regulatory requirements and data sensitivity classifications to inference workloads, determining which require sovereign (on-premises or private cloud) inference endpoints and informing workload placement decisions.

Classify prompts and responses by sensitivity (public, internal, confidential, restricted). Map regulatory requirements (GDPR, HIPAA, industry-specific) to specific inference workloads. Identify cross-border data flow restrictions for each deployment region. Conduct gap analysis between current cloud-only processing and privacy requirements. Define decision criteria for which workloads require sovereign inference. Apply the three-dimensional sovereignty model (data sovereignty, model sovereignty, inference sovereignty) from Forbes analysis.

Treating sovereignty as binary (all sovereign or all cloud) instead of applying appropriate sovereignty levels per workload. Underestimating the scope of data flowing through inference endpoints including prompts, responses, and usage metadata. Relying solely on cloud provider certifications without independent verification of data residency.

activities.name: Define Inference Service Level Objectives
activities.description: Establish quantitative SLOs with burn-rate alerting for inference services.

narratives.name: SLO Definition Technique
narratives.description: How quantitative performance targets with burn-rate alerting govern inference service quality.

narrativeContexts.context: Define Inference SLOs establishes quantitative performance targets for self-hosted inference services using SLO burn-rate alerting with multi-window configurations, providing the criteria against which performance assurance is measured.

Define SLOs based on managed API baseline measurements -- TTFT p99 under 500ms at peak load, zero sustained queuing, availability above 99.9%, error rate below 0.1%. Configure SLO burn-rate alerting with fast burn (1 hour window for critical) and slow burn (6 hour window for warning). Document on-call procedures specific to inference workload characteristics including GPU startup latency and model loading time. Define escalation paths for capacity versus performance versus hardware failure scenarios.

Setting SLOs without empirical baseline data from managed API performance. Using generic web service SLOs that do not account for GPU-specific characteristics. Implementing cause-based alerting that generates noise without actionable insights.

patterns.description: Orchestrates the progressive extension of AI inference from managed APIs to production-scale self-hosted infrastructure.

patternViews.name: Plan
patternViews.description: Assess opportunity and capture managed API baseline.

narrativeContexts.context: The planning phase captures quantitative telemetry from managed API consumption, validates the economic and strategic case for extending inference reach, identifies privacy and sovereignty requirements, and defines performance targets that self-hosted inference must meet.

activities: Map Model Requirements to Open-Weight Equivalents

narrativeContexts.context: The design phase translates baseline assessment into actionable plans -- mapping managed API models to open-weight equivalents, engineering GPU hardware profiles, classifying workloads into four tiers with migration wave assignments, and assessing risk impact and likelihood with mitigation strategies.

patternViews.name: Build
patternViews.description: Deploy inference infrastructure with models serving.
activities: Deploy Model Registry and Storage Infrastructure

narrativeContexts.context: The build phase deploys core inference infrastructure alongside managed APIs -- provisioning GPU-enabled clusters, deploying model registry and storage, configuring KServe model serving with vLLM, establishing observability, and achieving initial performance parity with managed API baselines.

patternViews.name: Test
patternViews.description: Validate governance, security, and performance parity.
activities: Implement API Gateway and Governance Layer
Enforce Tenant Isolation and Security Controls

narrativeContexts.context: The test phase validates governance, security, and operational integration -- deploying Connectivity Link with token-based rate limiting, enforcing namespace isolation through penetration testing, validating disaster recovery within RTO targets, and executing parallel-run validation for pilot workloads before production traffic cutover.

patternViews.name: Deploy
patternViews.description: Scale production workloads across multiple waves.
activities: Integrate Application Code for Dual-Endpoint Access

narrativeContexts.context: The deploy phase progressively extends production workloads through Waves 2-4 -- conversational agents, RAG applications, and high-volume APIs -- applying model compression systematically, optimizing performance through targeted tuning, and building team capability through hands-on operation of increasingly complex workloads.

The maintain phase deploys advanced architectures (llm-d prefix-cache-aware scheduling, disaggregated prefill-decode execution), continuously refines workload placement based on production telemetry, achieves transparent routing where applications switch backends through configuration only, and establishes the Community of Practice for organizational knowledge sharing.
